- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3), model frequently fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–4 days following negative sentiment.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 85% of 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.00 patterns, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overconfidence in flat sentiment periods.
